paper_title: Dark Matter Search with a Resonantly-Coupled Hybrid Spin System
notes: Paper presents new broadband constraints on axion-neutron (g_ann) and axion-proton (g_app) couplings using a K-Rb-21Ne hybrid spin system. Two regimes utilized: self-compensation (SC) at low frequencies [0.01-6 Hz] and hybrid spin resonance (HSR) at higher frequencies [3-1000 Hz]. For axion-neutron coupling, best limit is |g_ann| ≤ 3×10^-10 GeV^-1 in [2×10^-2, 4] Hz range, surpassing astrophysical limits and providing strongest laboratory constraints in [10, 100] Hz range. For axion-proton coupling, best terrestrial constraints achieved in [2×10^-2, 5] Hz and [16, 7×10^2] Hz ranges. Data points extracted from Fig. 4 and text statements; values are approximate read-offs from the exclusion plot. DM density ρ_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 from Standard Halo Model. Stochastic effects of DM accounted for in analysis. Post-analysis rejected all 62 candidate signals at 95% CL after rigorous testing (two-stage joint-LLR, signal-strength-stability, signal-shape analysis). One candidate at 46.704996 Hz marginally excluded. | selector: text (sole candidate)
